messages.body_plain:
Currently (and only temporarily), changeRangeR is off CRAN so it will need to be installed via github:

library(devtools)
devtools::install_github("https://github.com/wallaceEcoMod/changeRangeR")
library(changeRangeR)

For information, see the publication <https://doi.org/10.1111/csp2.12863>. changeRangeR also has two vignettes that may be helpful.
Single Species Analyses: https://wallaceEcoMod.github.io/changeRangeR/singleSpeciesMetrics.html
Biodiversity Metrics: https://wallaceEcoMod.github.io/changeRangeR/BiodivMetrics.html

changeRangeR is also available within the developmental version of wallace ("v3"). This can also be installed via github. Keep in mind, this is a developmental version as we continue to improve its functionality. You may need to install the archives of the `rgeos`, `rgdal`, and `maptools` packages to get v3 to work, as we are in progress in removing these expired packages.

library(devtools)
devtools::install_github("https://github.com/wallaceEcoMod/wallace/tree/biomodelos")

messages.body_plain:
I think the problem might simply be with the line:
occs_path <- ""
You need to enter your file path between the quotation marks. This is setting the path to where the file is located. Control-Click-Option on a Mac or Shift-Right Click on a PC gives the option to "copy as a pathname" which can be pasted.
Example: occs_path <- "Users/YourName/OccRecords/"

Otherwise the issue might be with the definition of the separators and decimals. Check your csv file to make sure that it matches as you have it set (the commas(,) as the separator and periods(.) as the decimals).

Bethany

messages.body_plain:
You need more than one variable to build a model. So if you wanted to use your landcover file with, say, climate data, you'll need them to be in the same folder so you can select them all.
If you wanted to use the file with Worldclim data, you'll have to download the bioclimatic variables externally (from the WorldClim site) and use the User Data module to upload all the files. It is currently not possible to select one single file, upload it, and then select another. You'll have to drag and select them all at once (at least three are needed to build a model).

messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I am researching the effect of climate change on deer (Odocoileus).

Please,

Quitting from lines 419-430 [unnamed-chunk-18] (wallace-session-2023-11-28.Rmd)  Error in `image.default()`: ! no slot of name "pnt" for this object of class "SpatRaster" Backtrace: 1. ecospat::ecospat.plot.niche(...) 3. graphics::image.default(...) Execution halted

### Environmental space

Calculating the part of environmental space more densly populated by
species & the availability of environmental conditions in the background
for *ODOCOILEUS hemionus* & *ODOCOILEUS virginianus*

```{r}
# Create density grid
espace_occDens_Pc_Pm <- espace_occDens(
  sp.name1 = "ODOCOILEUS hemionus",
  sp.name2 = "ODOCOILEUS virginianus",
  pca = espace_pca_Pc_Pm)
# Plots
graphics::par(mfrow = c(1,2))
ecospat::ecospat.plot.niche(espace_occDens_Pc_Pm[["ODOCOILEUS hemionus"]],
                            title = "ODOCOILEUS hemionus")
ecospat::ecospat.plot.niche(espace_occDens_Pc_Pm[["ODOCOILEUS virginianus"]],
                            title = "ODOCOILEUS virginianus")
```

Thanks in advance,

Eliécer
